the gate rethought.

**Revert needs no new env knob:** raise this threshold to `4` (the maximum
level macOS reports) and the gate's exit 1 verdict, the pressure check, can
never fire, since the comparison is `<=`. Raising the threshold does not
touch exit 2, the probe-failure verdict: when the sysctl can't be read or
parsed, the script exits 2 no matter what `--max-level` is set to, and the
task still reroutes off qwen. There is no env knob for that path. The actual
remedy is to fix the probe (make `kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level`
readable again) or mark the affected tasks `qwen_eligible: false` so routing
never reaches row 4. This works ONLY because the routing row reads
`--max-level` from this section explicitly, at dispatch time.

**Not guarded by `_AUTOPILOT_ESCALATION`** (unlike the qwen capability
breaker below): this is a host-safety mechanism, not a quality mechanism, and
keeps firing even under `_AUTOPILOT_ESCALATION=legacy`.

## Ordering

There are TWO separately-scoped orderings, NOT one single linear chain:

1. **Routing-time order** (per task, at implementor selection): qwen breaker
   consult -> memory-pressure gate -> qwen infra preflight -> dispatch. A
   tripped breaker short-circuits before the memory-pressure gate and the
   preflight; a memory-pressure gate fire short-circuits before the
   preflight.
2. **Failure-classification rule** (at the gate, or on a lost result): infra
   failure -> fall back same tier; capability failure -> diagnose, where
   **repair precedes escalate**.

Do NOT collapse these into a single `infra > breaker > repair > escalate`
chain. They are scoped to different moments.

## Kill-switches

- `_AUTOPILOT_ESCALATION=legacy`: read by `/autopilot:work` step 5.5. When set to
  `legacy`, skips diagnosis, repair, escalation, attribution stamping, AND the
  qwen capability breaker; the escalation machinery becomes byte-identical to
  pre-00065 (today's same-tier "max 2 implementation retries" cap). The
  memory-pressure gate (routing row 4) is not disabled by this knob and keeps
  firing under `legacy` (see § Memory gate). The codex rung interception
  (`/autopilot:work` step 3, § Codex rung) never fires under `legacy`: routing is the
  pre-00077 qwen/Claude-only path. The qwen one-shot carve-out (qwen
  fail -> Claude Sonnet) still applies. Any other value or absent -> the new
  flow.
- `_PLAN_TASKS_FLOOR=legacy` (alias: `sonnet`): read by `/autopilot:plan-tasks`,
  plan-time only — no `/autopilot:work` dispatch-time effect. Currently a documented
  no-op: the classifier rule-widening this knob was built to revert was
  withdrawn after review, so the `legacy` row and the current row of the
  step 4.7 tier classifier are identical — setting it changes nothing today.
  Any other value or absent -> the same (unchanged) classifier row. It is
  read by no script: `classify_tier.py` never consults it, so it does not
  guard the `_MECHANICAL_MAX_*` constants; reverting a tuned constant is a
  `git revert` of the accepting commit.
- `_AUTOPILOT_MODEL_BUILD=<model>`: the pre-existing env override, and the
  sonnet-first kill-switch (PRD 00076). Setting it forces every build launch
  to that model regardless of promotion signals.
- The Fable rescue has **no env knob**. It is gated by human approval
  (`autoclaude approve-fable <prd>`), one request per PRD ever, and `fable` is
  never a session model (§ Fable rescue).
- `_WORK_CODEX_RUNG=off`: read by `/autopilot:work` step 3. Disables the codex rung
  interception entirely; routing is byte-identical to pre-00077. Any other
  value or absent -> rung active.
- No decay knob exists. PRD 00111 reserved one and then did not need it:
  `_AUTOPILOT_MODEL_BUILD` already pins every build launch to a chosen model,
  which overrides decay and promotion alike (§ Decay).

## Tuning

`skills/run-autopilot/scripts/tune_routing.py` reads
`docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/ledger/attempts.jsonl` and writes
`docs/dev/project-management/audit-results/routing-proposal-<date>.md` (plus a `.patch` when
the mechanical row's line budget should halve). It proposes only: every
signal needs 12 rows before it moves, and it never edits a rule surface or
sets a kill-switch. The operator applies a proposal by hand and reverts it
with `git revert`.

## Decay

Escalation without decay is a ratchet, and every silent ratchet refunds the
savings the cheaper defaults earned. These rows are the single statement of
which build-phase promotion signals stop firing when their cause passes
(PRD 00111). They govern `build_model` in `cli/routing.py` (since PRD 00106);
the signals themselves are specified in `state-schema.md` § Build-phase model
routing.

**The loop recomputes, never remembers.** There is no stored promotion
latch anywhere: `build_model` re-derives the launch model from
current state at every relaunch. A live signal therefore decays by
construction the moment its state field clears — the rows below say when that
happens, they do not add a second mechanism.

| Signal | Class | Clears when |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| 1. frontmatter `session_model: opus` | sticky | Never automatically. Declared author intent; only editing the PRD removes it. (`default_model: opus` floors the task tier and drives no session since PRD 00200.) |
| 2. `replan_count > 0` | live | Phase 9 step 10 resets it to 0 at PRD completion. Within a PRD it is monotonic, so the promotion holds for that PRD's remaining sessions. |
| 3a. `stall_reason != null` | live | `/autopilot:run-autopilot` clears the field once it handles the stall. This is the one signal that already decayed before this PRD. |
| 3b. durable stall in the deferred logs | live | The stall ages out of the 2-newest-file window as later batches write their own logs. |
| 4. `cap_rotations` non-empty | live | Phase 9 step 10 clears it at PRD completion. Monotonic within a PRD, like signal 2. |
| 5. fable rescue ledger key | sticky | Never. A human approved an expensive rescue for that PRD; un-promoting it would spend the approval and then withhold the model it bought. |

**Signal 6 (repeat build session) is retired.** It fired whenever the target
had any prior `phase_launched: "build"` line in the metrics tail, which is
true of every PRD from its second session onward — so sonnet-first only ever
applied to session 1 and every multi-session PRD ran Opus regardless of how it
was going. It was also redundant: a repeat session caused by something going
wrong already trips signal 2, 3a or 4, and a repeat session caused merely by
a PRD having many tasks is exactly the case where Opus is not warranted.
Retiring it is what makes sonnet-first real for sessions 2+.

**Cross-PRD containment.** Signals 2, 3a and 4 fire only when `state.prd`
equals the resolved target, so the PRD that just finished cannot promote the
next one on its leftover scratch. Nothing escalation-related survives a
PRD-to-PRD reset.

**Task tiers decay separately** and are contained by construction: `/autopilot:work`
re-evaluates its routing table for every claimed task from that task's own
`model`, with no session-level memory, so a task escalated to opus
never changes the tier any other task dispatches at (`work` SKILL.md
§ Deterministic routing table).

**Reverting decay** needs no new knob: `_AUTOPILOT_MODEL_BUILD=claude-opus-5[1m]`
pins every build launch to Opus imm

# Rework Mode (step 1.5)

Moved verbatim out of `SKILL.md` step 1.5 (PRD 00119-v2; situational: read only
when `state.rework_task_ids` is a non-empty array). SKILL.md keeps the two-mode
filter table; the lifecycle, attempt-field and abort semantics live here.
**Read this file before the first task of a rework pass.**

**In rework mode, each task's status is set to `in_progress` at start** via `task-start` (overwriting whatever the prior status was — `pending` after Phase 6's reset, or `completed` on a defensive re-entry) and to `completed` at end — same lifecycle as a default-mode pass, so the dashboard reflects rework progress. `task-start` does not recompute `tasks_completed`, so reopening a previously-`completed` task leaves the count transiently stale until that task's next `task-done` recomputes it — accepted, not a bug to fix.

**In rework mode, the Attempt logging entry** (see `SKILL.md` § Attempt logging) sets `review_cycle` to the current `state.cycle` value (not null), `model` to the escalated tier read from `state.tasks[i].model` (set by `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 6), and `outcome` to `"completed"` or `"aborted"` as normal. It also **copies `state.tasks[i].escalation_reason` and `state.tasks[i].escalated_from` onto the entry when present** — Phase 6 sets them (`escalation_reason: "review_flag"`, `escalated_from: <prev_tier>`) on the review-flag escalation path, and this copy is how `review_flag` actually reaches `attempts[]` (the PRD metric "every escalation records reason in attempts[]" depends on it). Absent (a non-escalated rework re-dispatch) → omit both.

**`/autopilot:work` does NOT modify `rework_task_ids` itself.** Clearing is `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 6's responsibility, after this `/autopilot:work` invocation returns. **If `/autopilot:work` aborts mid-rework** (context overrun, Subagent Dispatch Budget overrun, unrecoverable error), `rework_task_ids` survives in state — this is correct recovery behavior: the next `/autopilot:run-autopilot` session resumes with the same rework batch and re-attempts the listed tasks at their already-escalated tier. Phase 6's clear runs only on the successful `/autopilot:work` return.

Cross-reference: `run-autopilot/references/state-schema.md` `rework_task_ids` row; `run-autopilot/references/phase-review.md` Phase 6 (rework) tier-escalation rule.

## Micro lane (PRD 00148)

Below a certain size the per-task ceremony costs more than the edit: a two-finding prose trim measured ~15 min and ~100K subagent tokens for a -25 net-line change. This lane spends none of that. It is a rework-only shortcut — a default-mode task has no findings block to size and no tests yet.

**Eligibility.** Read the task's `### Findings (verbatim)` block, collect one severity and one file path per line, and call `micro_lane_eligible(severities, files, in_rework=True)` from `scripts/work_routing.py`: at most two findings, at most two distinct files (the `:line` suffix is stripped), none CRITICAL, block parsed at all. Then run `git status --porcelain` and require every named file to be clean at claim time — the lane's escape hatch is `git checkout --`, which would destroy a live edit of the user's. Either check failing means the normal lane, unchanged.

**What it skips.** Steps 2.7, 2.8, 2.85, 2.9 and 2.95: no Tess, no Devon, no test commit, no red check. The orchestrator makes the change itself with the **Edit tool only** — no subagent, no `sed`, no shell rewrite.

**The overrun ceiling.** The 2/2 bound is a guess about the diff, made before the diff exists. This is the measurement that settles it. Before staging, over the working tree:

```bash
git diff --shortstat HEAD -- <files>
```

Compute `net_lines = insertions - deletions` and `file_count` (the step-5.6 formula). `net_lines >= 30` OR `file_count > 2` is an **overrun**: the task was not micro after all. description: Use when running Anthropic Claude Sonnet via the native claude CLI (headless) for code analysis, refactoring, or editing. Triggers on "run sonnet", "sonnet analyze", "ask sonnet".
compatibility: "Host-independent dispatch recipe requiring the named external model CLI and the bundled helper scripts."
---

# Sonnet Skill Guide

Sonnet is accessed via the native `claude` CLI (headless `-p`). The helper script defaults to the `sonnet` alias (latest base Sonnet) and exposes `-m/--model` for explicit overrides. This uses your Claude quota, not Copilot credits - never route Sonnet (or any model Claude already provides) through `copilot`.

## Dependencies

- Files read from other skill dirs:
  `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/use-codex/references/dispatch-contract.md` - mandatory,
  applies verbatim (see below)
  - `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/detect_usage_limit.py` - optional,
    for a deterministic reset-epoch parse of a usage-limit banner (see
    "Usage-limit banner" below)
- CLIs: `claude` (native, headless `-p`); `mise` for resolution

## Dispatch Contract (shared)

Background dispatch and waiting (TaskOutput-only waiting), following up, error handling, and the always-use-`-f` prompt rule are defined once in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/use-codex/references/dispatch-contract.md`. Read it before dispatching; it applies verbatim to this skill.

## Usage-limit banner (claude backend only)

`claude -p` is the one backend that can hit the **Claude usage limit** mid-run: instead of a normal result it returns a banner like `You've hit your session limit · resets 8:10pm (Europe/Prague)` (also `weekly`/`usage` limit; a stream-json run additionally carries a rejected `rate_limit_event` with a machine-readable `resetsAt` epoch). This is neither a task failure nor retryable — the quota is spent until the reset.

**Detect** it by scanning the run's output / `-o` file for the same markers `detect_usage_limit.py` uses: `hit your (session|usage|weekly) limit` or `usage limit reached`, and `resets <HH[:MM]> <am|pm> (<tz>)` for the reset time. For a deterministic reset epoch, run `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/detect_usage_limit.py --log <the -o output file>` — exit 0 prints the reset epoch (it parses both the prose banner and a stream-json `resetsAt`); exit 1 means no live limit.

**On a hit:** mark the run **FAILED**, report the reset time in the run report (`usage limit; resets <time>`), and do NOT retry before the reset — a retry re-fails identically. Under autopilot the `autoclaude` wrapper already sleeps-until-reset at the loop boundary; a standalone `use-sonnet` run cannot wait, so it stops and surfaces the reset for the user.

## Model Policy

- **Default:** `sonnet` (latest base Sonnet). Use unless the user asks for a different model.
- **`-m/--model` override:** pass a `claude` alias (`opus`, `haiku`) or a full model id (`claude-sonnet-5`). Opus costs more of your Claude quota - confirm with the user before defaulting to it for routine work.

## Running a Task

1. Select the permission mode required for the task; default to no special flags (interactive approval) unless edits are necessary.
2. Assemble the command with appropriate options:
   - `-m, --model MODEL` to override the default (`sonnet`); ask the user first if the override is a costlier tier (e.g. `opus`)
   - `-f, --file FILE` to read the prompt from a file (preferred - avoids shell escaping)
   - `-i, --interactive <prompt>` for interactive mode with initial prompt
   - `-a, --allow-edits` to auto-approve file edits only (maps to `--permission-mode acceptEdits`; Bash and other tools stay gated, so an unattended agentic child can stall on a prompt)
   - `-y, --yolo` for full permissions (`--permission-mode bypassPermissions`); REQUIRED for unattended agentic dispatches that must run commands. Note: a `-y` child runs with no warden or hook filtering
   - `-d, --dir <DIR>` to allow access to specific directories (maps to `--add-dir`)
   - `-s, --silent` accepted for compatibility (claude `-p` output is already clean)
3. When continuing a previous session, use `-c`/`--continue` or `-r`/`--resume [sessionId]`.
4. Run the command, capture output, and summarize the outcome for the user.
5. **After Sonnet completes**, inform the user: "You can resume this session with 'sonnet resume' or 'claude --continue'."

### Quick Reference

| Use case | Key flags |
| --- | --- |
| Read-only analysis | `-f prompt.txt` |
| Interactive with initial prompt | `-i "prompt"` |
| Auto-approve edits only | `-a -f prompt.txt` |
| Full auto, unattended agentic (edits + commands) | `-y -f prompt.txt` |
| Allow specific directory | `-d <DIR> -f prompt.txt` |
| Resume recent session | `--continue` |
| Resume specific session | `--resume [sessionId]` |
| Scripting (clean output) | `-s -f prompt.txt` |

## Helper Script

```bash
# Write prompt to temp file (see the shared dispatch contract), then run
bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -f /tmp/sonnet-prompt.txt

# With auto-approve edits (Bash still gated)
bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -a -f /tmp/sonnet-prompt.txt

# Override model (only after user approval - costlier tier)
bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -m opus -f /tmp/sonnet-prompt.txt

# Full permissions
bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -y -f /tmp/sonnet-prompt.txt

# Resume session
bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -r

# Capture output to file
bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -a -o /tmp/result.txt -f /tmp/sonnet-prompt.txt
```

Run `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh --help` for all options.

Background dispatch and waiting (TaskOutput-only waiting), following up, error handling, and the always-use-`-f` prompt rule are defined once in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/use-codex/references/dispatch-contract.md`. Read it before dispatching; it applies verbatim to this skill.

## Usage-limit banner (claude backend only)

`claude -p` is the one backend that can hit the **Claude usage limit** mid-run: instead of a normal result it returns a banner like `You've hit your session limit · resets 8:10pm (Europe/Prague)` (also `weekly`/`usage` limit; a stream-json run additionally carries a rejected `rate_limit_event` with a machine-readable `resetsAt` epoch). This is neither a task failure nor retryable — the quota is spent until the reset.

**Detect** it by scanning the run's output / `-o` file for the same markers `detect_usage_limit.py` uses: `hit your (session|usage|weekly) limit` or `usage limit reached`, and `resets <HH[:MM]> <am|pm> (<tz>)` for the reset time. For a deterministic reset epoch, run `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/detect_usage_limit.py --log <the -o output file>` — exit 0 prints the reset epoch (it parses both the prose banner and a stream-json `resetsAt`); exit 1 means no live limit.

**On a hit:** mark the run **FAILED**, report the reset time in the run report (`usage limit; resets <time>`), and do NOT retry before the reset — a retry re-fails identically. Under autopilot the `autoclaude` wrapper already sleeps-until-reset at the loop boundary; a standalone `use-sonnet` run cannot wait, so it stops and surfaces the reset for the user.

## Model Policy

- **Default:** `sonnet` (latest base Sonnet). Use unless the user asks for a different model.
- **`-m/--model` override:** pass a `claude` alias (`opus`, `haiku`) or a full model id (`claude-sonnet-5`). Opus costs more of your Claude quota - confirm with the user before defaulting to it for routine work.

## Running a Task

1. Select the permission mode required for the task; default to no special flags (interactive approval) unless edits are necessary.
2. Assemble the command with appropriate options:
   - `-m, --model MODEL` to override the default (`sonnet`); ask the user first if the override is a costlier tier (e.g. `opus`)
   - `-f, --file FILE` to read the prompt from a file (preferred - avoids shell escaping)
   - `-i, --interactive <prompt>` for interactive mode with initial prompt
   - `-a, --allow-edits` to auto-approve file edits only (maps to `--permission-mode acceptEdits`; Bash and other tools stay gated, so an unattended agentic child can stall on a prompt)
   - `-y, --yolo` for full permissions (`--permission-mode bypassPermissions`); REQUIRED for unattended agentic dispatches that must run commands. Note: a `-y` child runs with no warden or hook filtering
   - `-d, --dir <DIR>` to allow access to specific directories (maps to `--add-dir`)
   - `-s, --silent` accepted for compatibility (claude `-p` output is already clean)
3. When continuing a previous session, use `-c`/`--continue` or `-r`/`--resume [sessionId]`.
4. Run the command, capture output, and summarize the outcome for the user.
5. **After Sonnet completes**, inform the user: "You can resume this session with 'sonnet resume' or 'claude --continue'."

### Quick Reference

| Use case | Key flags |
| --- | --- |
| Read-only analysis | `-f prompt.txt` |
| Interactive with initial prompt | `-i "prompt"` |
| Auto-approve edits only | `-a -f prompt.txt` |
| Full auto, unattended agentic (edits + commands) | `-y -f prompt.txt` |
| Allow specific directory | `-d <DIR> -f prompt.txt` |
| Resume recent session | `--continue` |
| Resume specific session | `--resume [sessionId]` |
| Scripting (clean output) | `-s -f prompt.txt` |

```bash
# Override model (only after user approval - costlier tier)

# Capture output to file

```

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.17.0] - 2026-11-04

### Added

- **sysup**: on macOS, `rustup update` runs before `mise upgrade` when `rustup` is installed, so the Rust toolchain stays current and mise's `cargo:` tools build with it.
- **gems**: wheels for Python 3.15 (macOS arm64, Linux x64 and arm64, Windows x64), so installing on 3.15 no longer needs a Rust toolchain; `pyyaml` and `xattr` publish no 3.15 wheels yet, so pip and uv build them from source on 3.15 (a C compiler is needed for `xattr`).
- **backup**: TTY runs show per-instance live progress and elapsed time, with input-byte percentages capped at 99% for Python archives and activity only for system tar; `--quiet` hides live status while preserving final results and summary counts.
- **backup**: `--jobs` controls concurrent archive instances (default three); cancellation stops new work, joins workers, stops tar and cleans temporary files while preserving completed results and backups; interruption exits with status 130.
- **backup**: `--plan` previews metadata-only run/skip/fail decisions, reasons and existing-output replacement markers; selected outputs share one timestamp and colliding paths are rejected before plan, run or dry-run execution. Missing inputs report the same errors as a run; a metadata error fails only its instance, keeping its expanded source, while preserving collision checks.
- **backup**: optional `items` bundle literal source-relative files and directories into one archive, preserving empty directories and symlinks while applying inherited exclusions and `.bkpignore` rules.
- **backup**: per-instance `inherit_excludes`, `exclude_remove` and `exclude_add` control inherited exclusions for archives and `--show-excludes`, which still lists the resolved patterns sorted.

### Changed

- **backup**: missing sources and bundles with no surviving members now warn and skip without touching previous archives; each run reports archived or previewed, skipped, and failed step counts. Existing non-directory sources, unreadable sources and unreadable selected items still fail instead of counting as missing; a skipped bundle names its source.

### Fixed

- **backup**: a bundle's `out` may now lie under `source` when it is outside every selected item (for example `~/.local/backup/settings.tar.gz` for `items: [.gitconfig, .npmrc]`); an `out` equal to or inside a selected item still fails in run, `--dry-run` and `--plan`.
- **backup**: progress returns to archiving when a failure after system tar finishes triggers the Python fallback.
- **backup**: interruption during submission or result collection preserves every instance's outcome and finishes cleanup without waiting for a lost completion notification.
- **sysup**: a `timeout` on a captured multi-command shell step now stops the whole step; before, only bash died and the command it was waiting on kept running. Such a step runs in its own process group, so Ctrl-C is forwarded to it, a terminal prompt it raises stops it until the timeout, and a command it runs as root through `sudo` is still out of reach and survives. Interactive steps and steps without a timeout are unchanged

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import tarfile
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from backup.capabilities.tar_archive import TarArchive

_OMITTED = object()


@pytest.fixture(params=["python-tarfile", "system-tar"])
def engine(request: pytest.FixtureRequest) -> str:
    return request.param


@pytest.fixture(params=["run", "dry_run", "plan"])
def mode(request: pytest.FixtureRequest) -> str:
    return request.param


def _outcome(source: Path, out: Path, engine: str, mode: str, items: object = _OMITTED) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    kwargs: dict[str, object] = {"label": "bundle", "source": str(source), "out": str(out), "engine": engine}
    if items is not _OMITTED:
        kwargs["items"] = items
    if mode == "plan":
        entry = TarArchive().plan(**kwargs)
        assert entry.status in {"run", "fail"}
        return entry.status == "run", entry.reason
    (result,) = list(TarArchive().run(**kwargs, dry_run=mode == "dry_run"))
    return result.success, result.message


def _snapshot(source: Path) -> dict[str, bytes | str | None]:
    return {
        str(path.relative_to(source)): (
            str(path.readlink()) if path.is_symlink() else path.read_bytes() if path.is_file() else None
        )
        for path in source.rglob("*")
    }


def _case_alias(directory: Path) -> Path:
    alias = directory.with_name(directory.name.swapcase())
    if not alias.exists() or not alias.samefile(directory):
        pytest.skip("case-alias containment requires a real case-insensitive filesystem")
    return alias


class TestBundleCaseContainment:
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("items", [None, _OMITTED], ids=["none", "omitted"])
    def test_whole_tree_rejects_output_beneath_source_case_alias_without_changes(
        self, tmp_path: Path, engine: str, mode: str, items: object
    ) -> None:
        source = tmp_path / "Source"
        source.mkdir()
        (source / "a").write_bytes(b"first selected file")
        (source / "other").write_bytes(b"second selected file")
        out = _case_alias(source) / "new" / "deep" / "archive.tar.gz"
        before = _snapshot(source)

        success, message = _outcome(source, out, engine, mode, items)

        assert success is False
        assert "inside source" in message
        assert "inside selected item" not in message
        assert str(out) in message
        assert _snapshot(source) == before

    def test_bundle_rejects_output_equal_to_source_case_alias_with_source_message(
        self, tmp_path: Path, engine: str, mode: str
    ) -> None:
        source = tmp_path / "Source"
        source.mkdir()
        (source / "a").write_bytes(b"first selected file")
        (source / "other").write_bytes(b"second selected file")
        out = _case_alias(source)
        before = _snapshot(source)

        success, message = _outcome(source, out, engine, mode, ["a", "other"])

        assert success is False
        assert "inside source" in message
        assert "inside selected item" not in message
        assert str(out) in message
        assert _snapshot(source) == before

    def test_distinct_hard_link_output_preserves_selected_bytes_and_archives_every_item(
        self, tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, engine: str, mode: str
    ) -> None:
        source = tmp_path / "source"
        source.mkdir()
        selected = source / "a"
        selected.write_bytes(b"first selected file")
        (source / "other").write_bytes(b"second selected file")
        out = source / "a-backup.tar.gz"
        out.hardlink_to(selected)
        assert out.samefile(selected)
        before = _snapshot(source)
        monkeypatch.chdir(source)

        success, _ = _outcome(source, Path(out.name), engine, mode, ["a", "other"])

        assert success is True
        assert selected.read_bytes() == b"first selected file"
        assert (source / "other").read_bytes() == b"second selected file"
        if mode == "run":
            with tarfile.open(out, "r:gz") as archive:
                assert set(archive.getnames()) == {"a", "other"}
                assert archive.extractfile("a").read() == b"first selected file"
                assert archive.extractfile("other").read() == b"second selected file"
        else:
            assert _snapshot(source) == before
            assert out.samefile(selected)

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("selected", ["a", "other"])
    def test_output_equal_to_selected_file_is_rejected_without_changes(
        self, tmp_path: Path, engine: str, mode: str, selected: str
    ) -> None:
        source = tmp_path / "source"
        source.mkdir()
        (source / "a").write_bytes(b"first selected file")
        (source / "other").write_bytes(b"second selected file")
        out = source / selected
        before = _snapshot(source)

        success, message = _outcome(source, out, engine, mode, ["a", "other"])

        assert success is False
        assert "inside selected item" in message
        assert str(out) in message
        assert _snapshot(source) == before

    def test_case_alias_of_selected_file_rejects_output_without_changes(
        self, tmp_path: Path, engine: str, mode: str
    ) -> None:
        source = tmp_path / "source"
        source.mkdir()
        selected = source / "Config"
        selected.write_bytes(b"selected settings")
        (source / "other").write_bytes(b"also selected")
        out = _case_alias(selected).with_name("config")
        before = _snapshot(source)

        success, message = _outcome(source, out, engine, mode, ["Config", "other"])

        assert success is False
        assert "inside selected item" in message
        assert str(out) in message
        assert str(selected) in message
        assert _snapshot(source) == before

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("error", ["output identity permission denied", "archive metadata access denied"])
    def test_output_identity_permission_error_fails_without_replacing_output(
        self, tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, engine: str, mode: str, error: str
    ) -> None:
        source = tmp_path.resolve() / "source"
        directory = source / "Config"
        directory.mkdir(parents=True)
        (directory / "settings").write_bytes(b"selected settings")
        (source / "other").write_bytes(b"also selected")
        sibling = source / "Config-backup"
        sibling.mkdir()
        out = sibling / "archive.tar.gz"
        out.write_bytes(error.encode())
        before = _snapshot(source)
        real_lstat = Path.lstat

        def denied_lstat(path: Path) -> os.stat_result:
            if path == out:
                raise PermissionError(error)
            return real_lstat(path)

        with monkeypatch.context() as patch:
            patch.setattr(Path, "lstat", denied_lstat)
            success, message = _outcome(source, out, engine, mode, ["Config", "other"])

        assert success is False
        assert error in message
        assert _snapshot(source) == before

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("selected", ["Config", "Profiles"])
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("out_rel", ["", "archive.tar.gz", "new/deep/archive.tar.gz"])
    def test_case_alias_of_selected_directory_rejects_output_without_changes(
        self, tmp_path: Path, engine: str, mode: str, selected: str, out_rel: str
    ) -> None:
        source = tmp_path / "source"
        directory = source / selected
        directory.mkdir(parents=True)
        (directory / "settings").write_bytes(b"selected settings")
        (source / "other").write_bytes(b"also selected")
        alias = _case_alias(directory)
        out = alias / out_rel if out_rel else alias
        if out_rel == "archive.tar.gz":
            out.write_bytes(b"previous archive")
        before = _snapshot(source)

        success, message = _outcome(source, out, engine, mode, ["other", selected])

        assert success is False
        assert "inside selected item" in message
        assert str(out) in message
        assert str(directory) in message
        assert _snapshot(source) == before

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("selected", ["Config", "Profiles"])
    def test_near_miss_sibling_allows_output_and_keeps_every_selected_item(
        self, tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, engine: str, mode: str, selected: str
    ) -> None:
        source = tmp_path / "source"
        directory = source / selected
        directory.mkdir(parents=True)
        (directory / "settings").write_bytes(selected.encode())
        (source / "other").write_bytes(b"second item")
        sibling = source / f"{selected}-backup"
        sibling.mkdir()
        out = sibling / "archive.tar.gz"
        out.write_bytes(b"previous archive")
        before = _snapshot(source)
        monkeypatch.chdir(sibling)

        success, _ = _outcome(source, Path(out.name), engine, mode, [selected, "other"])

        assert success is True
        if mode == "run":
            with tarfile.open(out, "r:gz") as archive:
                assert set(archive.getnames()) == {selected, f"{selected}/settings", "other"}
                assert archive.extractfile(f"{selected}/settings").read() == selected.encode()
                assert archive.extractfile("other").read() == b"second item"
        else:
            assert _snapshot(source) == before

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("out_parent", ["target", "link"])
    def test_final_symlink_items_allow_output_in_target_without_archiving_target_contents(
        self, tmp_path: Path, engine: str, mode: str, out_parent: str
    ) -> None:
        source = tmp_path / "source"
        target = source / "target"
        target.mkdir(parents=True)
        (target / "private").write_bytes(b"do not archive")
        (source / "link").symlink_to("target", target_is_directory=True)
        (source / "broken").symlink_to("absent")
        (source / "other").write_bytes(b"keep")
        out = source / out_parent / "archive.tar.gz"
        out.write_bytes(b"previous archive")
        before = _snapshot(source)

        success, _ = _outcome(source, out, engine, mode, ["link", "broken", "other"])

        assert success is True
        assert (target / "private").read_bytes() == b"do not archive"
        assert (source / "link").readlink() == Path("target")
        if mode == "run":
            with tarfile.open(out, "r:gz") as archive:
                members = {member.name: member for member in archive.getmembers()}
                assert set(members) == {"link", "broken", "other"}
                assert members["link"].issym()
                assert members["link"].linkname == "target"
                assert members["broken"].issym()
                assert members["broken"].linkname == "absent"
                assert archive.extractfile("other").read() == b"keep"
        else:
            assert _snapshot(source) == before

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        ("items", "message"),
        [
            ([], "items must not be empty"),
            (["Config", "../escape"], "invalid item '../escape': must be a relative path inside the source"),
            (["Config", None], "items must be a list of relative paths"),
        ],
    )
    def test_invalid_items_take_precedence_over_output_containment(
        self, tmp_path: Path, engine: str, mode: str, items: object, message: str
    ) -> None:
        source = tmp_path / "source"
        directory = source / "Config"
        directory.mkdir(parents=True)
        out = directory / "archive.tar.gz"
        out.write_bytes(b"previous archive")
        before = _snapshot(source)

        success, reason = _outcome(source, out, engine, mode, items)

        assert success is False
        assert reason == message
        assert _snapshot(source) == before
